chunk_findings.detail: `_older_binary_refusal` is only invoked under `if not check`. A run such as `ddflow pins regenerate --check` with a stale PATH `ddflow` older than the log will skip this guard and proceed to `PN.regenerate(check=True)`. In that mode the old binary still computes pin outputs with its old behavior (the bug reports a 27-vs-25 line-count difference), so `--check` can emit a false “pins out of date”/incorrect diff instead of the refusal promised for older binaries. The guard should apply regardless of `check`, with `check` only suppressing the subsequent write/record calls.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: A valid but malformed `.ddflow/local/skew-notice.json` such as `{"seen": null}` makes `_notice_due` crash. `json.loads(...).get("seen", [])` returns `None`, and the later `[*seen, tag]` raises `TypeError`, which is not caught by the surrounding `except OSError`. The docstring says an unreadable marker only means the notice may repeat, but this input crashes the command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log.py:_notice_due

chunk_findings.detail: `_SKEW_WARNED` is keyed only by `(version, highest, log_format)` and is checked and added before `root` is considered. In one Python process that opens logs for two checkouts A and B with the same skew key and `skew_notice = once`, B never gets a warning even though B’s per-project marker is empty. That contradicts the function’s “once per key per machine and project” contract; a long-running ddflow embedder or test runner that processes multiple project roots hides B’s first skew notice.

chunk_findings.detail: The added project component is only the raw path string, not a canonical filesystem identity. Previous finding #3 still holds for relative roots: in one process, `os.chdir("/work/a")` then `EventLog(Path("proj"), "me").append(...)` emits a skew notice; later `os.chdir("/work/b")` then `EventLog(Path("proj"), "me").append(...)` constructs the same `process_key`, so `_notice_due` returns `False` for project B even though B's `.ddflow/local/skew-notice.json` is empty. The fix only works when the two projects serialize to different root strings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log.py:_notice_due process_key = (*key, str(root or ""))

chunk_findings.detail: The process-global `_SKEW_WARNED` set now records one entry per distinct `str(root)` and is never pruned outside tests. A long-running ddflow embedder or CI worker that opens logs for many checkouts under the same skew will accumulate one entry per checkout indefinitely, so memory grows linearly with the number of distinct project roots. The old 3-tuple key did not have this unbounded per-project dimension; the change converts the cache into an unbounded leak in exactly the long-running case the fix is meant to support.
